summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, a history of hepatitis C, and prior osteosarcoma presented with a painful crisis characterized by band-like lower abdominal and left hip pain. She was treated with IV fluids and IV hydromorphone initially, transitioning to oral pain medication as her symptoms improved. Her hemoglobin dropped from 8.8 to 6.9 g/dL, but she declined transfusion due to prior transfusion-related hepatitis C; her levels stabilized at 7.1 g/dL with evidence of reticulocytosis. She remained afebrile without respiratory symptoms. A chest X-ray showed mild pulmonary edema and cardiac enlargement but no acute infection or acute chest syndrome. Hypotension was managed by holding lisinopril temporarily, later restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with stable pain control, instructions to stay hydrated, and follow-up plans with her hematologist and PCP.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of bone
